'''Victor Alexandrovich Kolyvagin''' ({{langx|ru|Виктор Александрович Колывагин}}, born 11 March, 1955) is a [[Russia|Russian]] mathematician who wrote a series of papers on [[Euler system]]s, leading to breakthroughs on the [[Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]], and [[Iwasawa theory|Iwasawa's conjecture]] for [[cyclotomic fields]].<ref>
{{cite book
|title=Euler Systems
|first=Karl
|last=Rubin
|series=Annals of Mathematics Studies
|publisher=Princeton University Press
|year=2000
|isbn=0-691-05075-9
|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gnNzIqlTbnkC&pg=PA3
}}</ref> His work also influenced [[Andrew Wiles]]'s work on [[Fermat's Last Theorem]].<ref name="science-1993"/><ref>
{{cite journal
|title=Getting a Grip on Elliptic Curves
|first=Barry A.
|last=Cipra
|authorlink= Barry Arthur Cipra
|journal=Science |series=New Series
|volume=243
|issue=4887
|date=January 6, 1989
|pages=30–31
|publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science Stable 
|jstor=1703169
|doi=10.1126/science.243.4887.30 
|pmid=17780417
|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.243.4887.30
|url-status=live
|archive-url=https://archive.today/20221105045450/https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.243.4887.30
|archive-date=2022-11-05|url-access=subscription
}}</ref>

==Career==
Kolyvagin received his Ph.D. in Mathematics in 1981 from [[Moscow State University]],<ref name="nyt=2002"/> where his advisor was [[Yuri I. Manin]]. He then worked at [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] in Moscow<ref name="science-1993">
{{cite journal
|title=Fermat Proof Hits a Stumbling Block 
|first=Barry 
|last=Cipra
|publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science 
|journal=Science
|year=1993 
|jstor=2882956 
|volume=263
|issue=5142
|doi=10.1126/science.262.5142.1967-a 
|pages=1967–8 
|bibcode=1993Sci...262.1967C 
}}</ref> until 1994. Since 1994 he has been a professor of mathematics in the [[United States]]. He was a professor at [[Johns Hopkins University]] until 2002 when he became the first person to hold the [[Mina Rees]] Chair in mathematics at the [[Graduate Center of the City University of New York]].<ref>
{{cite news
|author=Targeted News Service
|date=2009-12-22
|title=NSF Invests a Million Dollars in Number Theory at the CUNY Graduate Center}}</ref><ref name="nyt=2002">
{{cite news
|title=Benefactor's Chair Filled at CUNY
|first=Karen W. 
|last=Arenson 
|date=August 7, 2002 
|newspaper=The New York Times
|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/08/07/nyregion/bulletin-board-benefactor-s-chair-filled-at-cuny.html}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 1990 he received the {{Interlanguage link|Chebyshev Prize|lt=Chebyshev Prize|ru|Золотая медаль имени П. Л. Чебышёва}} of the [[USSR Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="nyt=2002"/>
